questions.q: The compliance audit created in the chapter (ComplianceAudit, TO FILE) uses which ON_FAILURE setting, and how does it differ from a pure monitoring audit?
options: ON_FAILURE = CONTINUE, to never interrupt workloads
ON_FAILURE = SHUTDOWN, to halt the server on audit failure
ON_FAILURE = FAIL_OPERATION, to fail the audited operation if the audit cannot write
ON_FAILURE = IGNORE, to silently drop events
questions.explain: The compliance audit uses WITH (ON_FAILURE = FAIL_OPERATION) because compliance requires the audit record to be guaranteed; a threat-detection audit can use CONTINUE since missing an event is less severe than blocking business operations.

questions.q: In the embedding-based schema drift detector, what cosine distance threshold flags an object as drifted from its baseline?
questions.explain: detect_schema_drift uses distance_threshold=0.15; a very high distance above 0.5 marks an object as likely entirely new rather than modified.

questions.q: Which vector store and embedding model does the chapter use for the compliance RAG pipeline?
options: Azure AI Search with ada-002 embeddings
ChromaDB with the text-embedding-3-large embedding function
questions.explain: setup_compliance_rag_store builds a ChromaDB collection named 'compliance_policies' using OpenAIEmbeddingFunction with model text-embedding-3-large to index policy documents and prior audit reports.

questions.q: In the chapter's two-stage PII column classification, which of these is a valid pii_category value returned by the LLM?
questions.explain: The allowed pii_category values are NONE, FINANCIAL, HEALTH, IDENTITY, CONTACT, BEHAVIORAL, and CREDENTIAL; FINANCIAL is one of them.

questions.q: The chapter's governance section ('audit the auditor') requires what for every LLM call that produces a compliance finding?
options: No logging, to reduce storage cost
Only the API cost logged for chargeback
The prompt, model version, response, and timestamp logged in an append-only table
questions.explain: Because auditors can ask how an exception was identified, the chapter requires logging every LLM call's prompt, model version, response, and timestamp in an append-only table with the same rigor as primary audit logs.
